qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Phase ten. Transformers and attention. This is how A I learned to pay attention.
The text is cut into pieces called tokens.
Text is cut into tokens.
Each token is looked up as a list of numbers.
Each token becomes a list of numbers.
The two copies of the word bank get exactly the same numbers.
The two banks get exactly the same numbers.
So nothing tells us which bank came first.
Nothing says which one came first.
So we add a position pattern to every token.
Add a position pattern to every token.
The two lists are added together, number by number.
Add them up, number by number.
Now the two banks are different, and ready for the model.
Now the two banks are different.
Imagine three words, with scores of two, one and zero.
Imagine three words, each with a score.
Stretch each score using e to its power, and the biggest grows most.
Stretch the scores: the biggest grows most.
Dividing by the total gives shares that add up to one.
Divide by the total: the shares add to 1.
Bigger gaps between the scores give a sharper split.
Bigger gaps give a sharper share-out.
Attention will use these shares in a moment.
Attention will use these shares.
In this sentence, the word it stands for a noun.
Which noun does “it” stand for?
It looks at every word in the sentence, itself included.
It looks at every word, itself included.
But some words matter more, so each gets a different share.
But some words matter more than others.
Its new meaning leans mostly on robot.
Its new meaning leans on “robot”.
Every word does this at the same time. For seven words, that is forty-nine shares.
Every word does this, all at the same time.
Each word makes a query, what it is looking for.
Query: what I am looking for.
It also makes a key, what it has to offer.
Key: what I have to offer.
Take the query of barked, and compare it with each key.
Compare the query of “barked” to each key.
For each key, multiply the pairs of numbers, then add them up.
Multiply the pairs, then add them up.
Dog matches best, with a score of three.
“dog” matches best: a score of 3.
Divide by one point four one, to keep the scores small.
Divide by 1.41 to keep scores small.
Softmax then turns the scores into shares.
Softmax turns them into shares.
Each word also carries a value, which is its content.
Each word also carries a value: its content.
Scale each value by its share, so dog counts the most.
Scale each value by its share.
Add the scaled values up, and barked gets a new set of numbers.
Add them up: new numbers for “barked”.
The same is done for every word at once.
Do it for every word at once.
So every word ends up with one new set of numbers.
One new set of numbers per word.
Attention runs in several heads, each with its own query, key and value.
Each head has its own query, key and value.
One head learns who it refers to.
One head learns what “it” means.
Another head looks at the word just before.
Another looks at the word before.
Other heads learn who acts, and what is acted on.
Others learn who acts and what is acted on.
Each head hands back sixteen numbers for every word.
Each head hands back 16 numbers per word.
Glued together, the four make sixty-four numbers.
Glued together, they make 64 numbers.
A layer has two parts, each wrapped in Add and Norm.
Two parts, each with Add & Norm.
Attention lets the words share information with each other.
Attention lets the words share information.
A skip path adds the part's output to its input.
A skip path adds output to input.
Norm then re-centres the numbers around zero, and rescales them.
Norm re-centres the numbers around zero.
The feed-forward network treats each word on its own.
The same network treats each word alone.
The shape in and out is the same, so layers can stack.
Same shape in and out, so layers stack.
To translate, the decoder starts from a start token.
Translating starts from a start token.
Every word it could write next gets a share.
Every possible next word gets a share.
The likeliest word is written down, as the start of the German sentence.
The likeliest word is written down.
Then it asks again, and writes the second word.
Then it asks again.
Masked attention stops a word peeking at later words.
Masked attention: no peeking at later words.
Each new word is added, and the loop goes round again, until the sentence is complete.
Append the word, then go round again.
When it writes the end token, the loop stops.
The end token stops the loop.
Transformers can read more than text. A picture can be cut into patches.
A picture can be cut into patches.
Each patch is a token, one hundred and ninety-six in all.
Each patch is a token: 196 in all.
Every token scores every token, which makes over thirty-eight thousand scores.
Every token scores every token: 196 × 196.
Halve the patch size, and there are four times as many tokens.
Half-size patches: four times the tokens.
But sixteen times as many scores, since the cost grows with the square.
But sixteen times the scores.
Attention weighs every word in the sentence.
Heads run side by side, and layers stack up.
The decoder writes one word at a time.
